facts.text: Taradale gets its name from a developer’s daughter, Tara, whose story is woven into the neighborhood’s early history.
The neighborhood sits on Calgary’s northeastern edge, bordered by Taradale Drive to the north, 68 Street E to the east, 64 Avenue N to the south, and Falconridge Boulevard to the west.
Taradale was annexed by Calgary in 1961 and officially established as a community in 1984, marking its transition from rural land to suburban development.
Residents enjoy one of Calgary’s safest neighborhoods, consistently ranking among the city’s lowest crime rates.
Local families send their children to Taradale Elementary School and Ted Harrison Middle School, two of the area’s primary public schools.
Most homes in Taradale are single‑family detached houses, with about ten percent of the housing stock available for rent.
